messages: Lina: quick design review — iterating on the 'traffic fade' rollout slider. need quick feedback on copy, screen-reader order, and rollback affordance. Ava: :eyes: looks nice visually. two immediate concerns: 1) SR announce order is weird when you keyboard-adjust the slider, 2) Rollback button feels dangerously close to Promote. Diego: probably because we're updating the whole slider container with aria-live. VoiceOver ignores some changes if the focus is on the input. move the live text to a dedicated span and update that only. Lina: can you paste a tiny example? Diego: sure — quick snippet: ```html Canary at 10% ``` Ava: that should help. also for keyboard + SR users, when they use arrow keys we should debounce announcements so VoiceOver doesn't queue a bunch of values. Matt: fwiw we need a fast path for SREs to rollback during incidents — single-click fallback is important. but we also need to prevent accidental clicks from product folks. brainstorm: hold-to-confirm for mouse, and a modal for keyboard? Sam: hold-to-confirm is tricky for accessibility. keyboard users need an equivalent. propose: keyboard trigger opens a small confirmation dialog (focus-trapped) with a clear heading and a primary 'Confirm rollback' button. mouse can use hold-to-confirm as a progressive enhancement. Ava: agreed. copy tweak: instead of 'Promote to 100%' maybe use 'Promote to full traffic' — '100%' is fine but some folks misread. also tooltip: 'Routes all traffic to this version. Rollback available in Version history.' Lina: proposal: primary button text = 'Promote to full traffic', secondary = 'Schedule rollout' (for timed rollouts), danger action = 'Rollback' with confirm modal. microcopy under the slider: 'Canary — gradual traffic over 10 minutes (editable)'. Matt: :thumbsup: add small inline note under timeline: 'Tip: Use left/right to scrub history, Enter to inspect version details'. Diego: perf note — timeline scrub currently redraws a lot (canvas). need to throttle redraw on keyboard scrub to stay responsive. I'll file an infra perf issue. Lina: filed PERF-1234. Accessibility order decision: when scrubbing version history we should announce in this order: 1) version label/id, 2) timestamp (relative), 3) status (live/rolled back), 4) available actions (promote, rollback). e.g. 'Version v1.4.2, deployed 3 hours ago, live, actions: promote, rollback'. Ava: I'll run VoiceOver + NVDA on the prototype tomorrow morning and report back. Matt: tiny language nit: 'Rollback' button tooltip could say 'Revert traffic to the previously active version' — more explicit. Sam: accessibility for focus order: make sure the rollback modal focuses the heading first and that the cancel button is first in DOM for keyboard natural flow. DeployBot: demo-deploy triggered by Lina on staging — preview URL: https://staging.redwood.internal/rollout/preview/2041250000 Lina: thanks everyone — I'll update the Figma with the copy changes and aria-live tweak. tagging follow-ups: @Diego for perf, @Ava for SR runs, @Sam for modal keyboard flow. Ava: thanks — will do SR pass and post a short checklist in this thread. :heart: Matt: great, ship it once SR + perf are green.
